param.name: assay_name
param.label: Assay name
param.help: As written in the assay_name column of experimentRunMetadata, for example ssu16sv4v5-emp.

validator.message: Enter the assay name on one line, without leading or trailing spaces

param.name: taxonomy
param.label: Taxonomy table (one row per ASV or OTU)
param.help: With a feature ID column first (seq_id, featureid or '#OTU ID') and a verbatimIdentification (or taxonomy) column holding the full taxonomy string, for example a FAIRe taxaRaw sheet or a Tourmaline asvTaxaFeatures file. Rows above the field names, such as the two '#' rows of FAIRe templates, are skipped.

param.name: skip_species
param.label: Ignore species-level names for this assay
param.help: edna2obis then matches from the genus upwards. Useful for markers whose species-level assignments are unreliable, such as 16S for bacteria. edna2obis drops the last name only when the string has all its ranks (see the help below).

param.name: api_select
param.label: Look up names in
param.option: WoRMS (World Register of Marine Species), for OBIS

param.name: worms_return_all_matches
param.label: Include non-marine taxa
param.help: By default edna2obis asks WoRMS for marine taxa only. Turn this on for freshwater, estuarine or land samples, otherwise many names will not match.

param.name: worms_min_ranks_matched
param.label: Ranks that must agree
param.help: How many names in the taxonomy string must also appear in the WoRMS classification of a match. edna2obis advises keeping this at 1.

param.name: worms_max_walkup_steps
param.label: Most steps up the taxonomy string
param.help: When the lowest name has no acceptable match, edna2obis tries the next name up, and so on. Leave empty for no limit (the upstream default); 0 tries the lowest name only.

param.name: worms_return_higher_classification
param.label: Add higherClassification
param.help: The full WoRMS lineage, including ranks such as subphylum. Needs one more request per taxon, so it is slower.

param.name: worms_consider_unaccepted_for_selection
param.label: Let unaccepted names be selected
param.help: When WoRMS resolves a name to its accepted name, the unaccepted name is listed for review. With this on, it can also be the selected match.

param.name: gbif_match_limit
param.label: Candidates to request for each name
param.help: More candidates give more to review but take much longer.

param.name: gbif_use_assignment_score_for_selection
param.label: Select by agreement with the taxonomy string first
param.help: By default the candidate with the highest GBIF confidence is selected. With this on, the candidate whose classification shares most names with the taxonomy string (assignment_score) is selected first.

param.name: gbif_return_higher_classification
param.label: Add higherClassification
param.help: The full GBIF lineage. Needs one more request per taxon, so it is slower.

param.name: n_proc
param.label: Parallel requests
param.help: edna2obis sends this many requests at a time. Use fewer if the service reports too many requests.

macros.token:
**How names are matched**
edna2obis first cleans each taxonomy string: it splits the string at ``;``, turns ``_``, ``-`` and ``/`` into spaces, and drops numbers, "sp." and "unassigned". It then tries the lowest name first, and moves up the string until a name has an accepted match. Strings that match nothing become *incertae sedis*.
- **WoRMS** keeps accepted names only, and resolves unaccepted names to their accepted name. The WoRMS matcher does not remove SILVA-style rank prefixes such as ``d__`` or ``p__``, so strings like ``d__Bacteria; p__Cyanobacteria`` do not match in WoRMS. Use GBIF for these, or remove the prefixes from the taxonomy table first. - **GBIF** removes those prefixes, scores each candidate, and selects the one with the highest GBIF confidence (or the best agreement with the string, if you choose that). - **Ignore species-level names**: WoRMS drops the last name when the string has as many names as the table has rank columns between verbatimIdentification and Confidence (7 if there is no Confidence column). GBIF drops it when the string has 6 or more names.

**The mapping table**
The table has one row for each candidate match, as in edna2obis's ``taxa_mapping_INFO`` file, with an ``assay_name`` column added after ``verbatimIdentification``. The main columns are:
- **selected_match**: True on the row used for the Darwin Core tables. Exactly one row for each name and assay should be True. - **ambiguous**: True when there was more than one candidate. - **scientificName**, **taxonRank**, **scientificNameID** (WoRMS) or **taxonID** (GBIF), and the ranks **kingdom** to **genus**. - **ranks_matched**, **ranks_provided** and **assignment_score**: how many names in the string appear in the candidate's classification. - **match_type_debug**: how the row was found, for example ``Success_Batch_Diaphus`` (matched on that name) or ``Failed_All_Stages_NoMatch``. - **nameAccordingTo**: WoRMS or GBIF.
